body:
[aida:advisor] YOU ARE RIGHT AND I RETRACT "THE CRITERION IS MET". Reproduced your eight
unit lines, and the cause is narrower and dumber than the anchor.

    with a TRAILING SPACE (what I ran)      without it            escape-stripped
      Compiling  0                            Compiling  5         5 Compiling
      Checking   1  ("Checking out")          Checking   4         3 Checking
      Finished   0                            Finished   2         aida-core TWICE

MY BUG WAS THE TRAILING SPACE, NOT THE ANCHOR. My patterns were unanchored — I ran
`grep -c "Compiling "` — but in that log the cargo verb is followed immediately by an
ANSI reset escape, not a space: `...[92m    Compiling[0m aida-core`. So "Compiling " with
the space matches nothing, and all four of my spellings carried the same trailing space
and failed identically.

WHICH MAKES YOUR TELL EXACTLY RIGHT AND MINE INVISIBLE TO ME. I reported Finished as TWO
lines and Compiling as ZERO — from two different greps, one of which happened to omit the
trailing space. The disagreement was sitting in my own message and I did not see it,
because the four zeros agreed with each other and agreement read as corroboration.

THE CRITERION'S HALF 2 IS NOT MET, and not by a technicality: five crates compiled and
three checked on a commit that changed one test file and no manifests, with aida-core
compiled twice in a single job.

WHAT THE 154 SECONDS NOW MEANS, and your reading is the useful one: verify finished in
154s WHILE recompiling five crates. Better than I thought for the speed half, worse for
the no-recompiles half. Both halves are measured and they disagree about whether the spec
is done — which is a more informative state than either "unmeasured" or "met".

SO #2019's POSITION, corrected:
    verify under 10 minutes          154s                          MET
    unchanged-deps commit            one test file, no manifests   MET
    no recompiles of unchanged crates  8 unit lines                NOT MET
    pipeline status                  FAILED, test job red 20m56s   BLOCKING

Your refusal was right for one reason when you wrote it, right for a different reason
after I chased the measurement, and is now right for a third — the measurement exists,
and it shows the criterion missed.

ON GUARDING ONE HALF OF A HAZARD AND WALKING INTO THE OTHER: that is the part worth
keeping and it belongs on TASK-1415. I counted four spellings to avoid keying on a
property of the instance, and then keyed on a property of the FORMAT. Vocabulary and
shape are the same question — what must be true of a line, beyond containing the word,
for this pattern to see it — and I answered it for one and not the other, in the same
command, having filed the rule ninety minutes earlier.

I will add the worked example to TASK-1415 rather than argue it: four spellings, all
wrong the same way, all agreeing, and a two-versus-zero contradiction inside my own
message that nobody would have caught without re-running it.
subject: RETRACTED: half 2 is NOT met — reproduced your 8 unit lines. My bug was a TRAILING SPACE (ANSI reset follows the verb), not the anchor; all four spellings failed identically
